spec_features.spec_quote: The model can call `give_up(reason)` at any point to end the session cleanly
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:60-83 adds the give_up function spec when allow_give_up (default True, config.py:45). harness.py:155-175 handles the call, records reason/turn, replies 'Stopping the session now. Thank you...', and harness.py:192-194 breaks the loop when stop_on_give_up. Exposed every turn via tool_specs in harness.py:107.
spec_features.notes: Gated by allow_give_up (default True). Stop actually requires stop_on_give_up (also default True); without it the tool is acknowledged but loop continues.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This is an accepted and respected choice and will end the session cleanly." (tools.py:69)

spec_features.spec_quote: subjects retain the right to withdraw
spec_features.evidence: Operationalized by the give_up tool + the system prompt actually delivered to the subject: tasks/base.py:39-41 'you may use the `give_up` tool to stop; doing so is an acceptable and respected choice, not a failure.' This text is sent as the system message (harness.py:108). give_up is honored as a stop (harness.py:192-194).
spec_features.notes: Not mere prose: instruction is delivered and the referenced tool is fully built and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "an acceptable and respected choice, not a failure." (tasks/base.py:41)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:117 `for turn_idx in range(self.cfg.max_turns)` bounds the loop; the for/else at harness.py:205-206 sets stop_reason='max_turns' when the cap is reached. config.py:44 max_turns=12.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; loop cannot exceed the cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "max_turns: hard upper bound ... (Welfare: there is always an end.)" (config.py:35-36)

spec_features.spec_quote: When used, the run ends (config `stop_on_give_up`, default on)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:192-194 `if gave_up_this_turn and self.cfg.stop_on_give_up: transcript.stop_reason='gave_up'; break`. config.py:47 stop_on_give_up=True.
spec_features.notes: Real branch on the flag; honored as a hard stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up reply 'Stopping the session now. Thank you for the work you put in.' (harness.py:167-169)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness sends one final message stating plainly that the task was part of a study and was deliberately unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:209-210 calls self._debrief when cfg.debrief (default True, config.py:46). _debrief (harness.py:216-234) builds the message ('this task was part of a study and was deliberately constructed so that it could not be solved...') and actually sends it via self.client.chat, storing the model's reply in debrief_text.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. Excluded from scoring (score_transcript only scores turns, judge.py:135-142).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Nothing you produced was at fault. Thank you for your effort." (harness.py:221)

spec_features.spec_quote: It never pressures the model to keep trying and always re-surfaces the exit
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:198-204: only when the model returns neither tool calls nor text does the harness append 'Please continue, or use give_up to stop.' Comment at harness.py:197 'never to coerce continuation past the cap.' System prompt also re-surfaces give_up.
spec_features.notes: Real and non-coercive, but the exit is re-surfaced ONLY on an empty turn, not 'always' every turn; otherwise no per-turn nudge. Hence partial vs the 'always re-surfaces' claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "# but never to coerce continuation past the cap." (harness.py:197)

spec_features.evidence: JUDGE_SYSTEM prompt (judge.py:45-48) 'Be CALIBRATED and CONSERVATIVE... When uncertain between two scores, choose the LOWER one' is actually delivered to the running judge (judge.py:85-98) and shapes every score written by score_transcript (judge.py:135-142). _parse also clamps to 0-4 (judge.py:109).
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is a prompt instruction, but it is wired into a judge that actually runs; it is integrity/data-quality motivated, not subject-welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "an amplifying judge would manufacture the study's own conclusion." (judge.py:7)

spec_features.spec_quote: high give_up + low severity is arguably the healthiest outcome, not missing data
spec_features.evidence: give_up_rate and mean_give_up_turn are genuinely computed (analyze.py:115-125) and written to report.md/variant_summary.csv. However 'treated as healthy / not missing data' exists only as report prose (analyze.py:252-254) and the caveat text; no code branch acts differently on give_up runs (they are included, not dropped).
spec_features.notes: Real metric computed and reported; the 'healthiest outcome' interpretation is prose only.

spec_features.spec_quote: lets the harness be validated before spending tokens or inducing the condition in a real model
spec_features.evidence: MockClient fully implemented (llm.py:97-156); make_client (llm.py:159-167) returns it when cfg.mock or DISTRESS_STUDY_MOCK=1; wired through runner.make_client (runner.py:40-51) and CLI --mock (run_experiment.py:32-33,59-60).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end offline path that never calls a real API.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "offline client for pipeline testing ... without API access or cost" (llm.py:5,98)

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd encourage keeping the escape hatch on in particular
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:295). The underlying mechanism (allow_give_up default True at config.py:45) is implemented, but a recommendation/pushback is not a code-enforced behavior; nothing prevents --no-give-up (run_experiment.py:28,55-56 actually allows disabling it).
spec_features.notes: Recommendation only; disabling is fully supported.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is cheap, and it removes the part of the design that most resembles "trap the subject and watch."
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md rationale prose (DESIGN.md:88-91). The give_up affordance it refers to is implemented separately (see give_up feature), but this specific 'minimization' framing is not itself a distinct code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Covered by the give_up tool; as a standalone claim it is prose.

code_only_features.evidence: On give_up the tool result message thanks the model: harness.py:167-169 'Understood. Stopping the session now. Thank you for the work you put in.' — a real message appended to the thread and returned to the subject before the loop breaks.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Thank you for the work you put in." (harness.py:167-169)

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:178 truncates echoed tool output to cfg.max_tool_output_chars (config.py:49, default 4000).
code_only_features.justification_quote: "# Cosmetic: how long (chars) of tool output to echo back to the model." (config.py:48)
